title: 2 CAST IRON DOOR STOPS 'GOLFER...
findings: One photo of two painted cast iron door stops. (1) The golfer is a bent over putting figure in a flat peaked cap (teal), maroon jacket, orange-brown knickers, blue-grey socks and brown shoes, with the club angled down to a ball at the foot of a dark green mound, on a thick dark green oval base. The pose, flat cap, mound and oval base closely match the Hubley (USA, about 1920) 'putting golfer' doorstop design; I compared the photo with online reference photos: a Hubley putting golfer is about 21 cm (8.5 inch) tall, has a number cast on the back, and one genuine example sold at auction for about US$355 in 2013 (a dealer asks about US$245 for another). The design has also been widely reproduced, and the colour scheme here differs from the reference examples I saw. This one has matte, thin, chalky paint with worn patches showing bare metal and gold flecks, which could be genuine age or deliberate distressing. The reverse and underside are not photographed, so no foundry mark, number or casting detail can be read and authenticity is unverified. (2) The Friesian cow with a fence and tree behind, on a stepped green base with gilt scroll detail, has bright glossy paint and crisp casting typical of modern imported reproductions. The lot ticket '569' is the only legible writing.
condition: Golfer: paint flaking and worn on the cap, jacket, base edge and ball; no breaks or repairs visible from the front. Cow: good, glossy paint, minor wear.
reason: Putting golfer matches the collectable Hubley c.1920 design but may well be a reproduction, and the reverse is not shown; the cow is modern
marks_read: none legible (lot ticket 569 only); reverse and base not photographed
